title: How Yahia Bakour built Stock Alarm and sold it for $500k on Acquire.com
summary: Yahia explains how he and his co-founders grew a B2C stock alert app mostly through community posting, ASO and SEO, then sold it for $500k after three years. He covers what he prioritized in a buyer (terms and head space over price), what buyers scrutinized in diligence, and how long the sale took.

principles.text: Get early customers by posting where your buyers already hang out, not just friends and family.
principles.quote: getting past just like the first dollar pretty much was all like posting uh where our customers would have hung out so at the time it was like Reddit or quora

principles.text: App Store keyword optimization and SEO can carry an app from friends-and-family to strangers finding it.
principles.quote: optimizing for certain keywords on the App Store worked really nicely uh bunch of SEO stuff

principles.text: Inbound feature requests are a product-market-fit signal: confirm they'd pay, ship fast, then prioritize.
principles.quote: they reach out they're like hey I'd love if you made this change or like if you if we make this change will you pay and then they'd be yes and that we make the change in like a couple days

principles.text: One sharp differentiator, like phone-call alerts, can hook users before you broaden the product.
principles.quote: the phone call feature was the main thing that kind of hooked people in

principles.text: B2C is painful early because you need many more paying customers than B2B to reach the same revenue.
principles.quote: getting past that first like 100 Mr instead of it being one customer it's 20 right so it just a lot more pain initially

principles.text: When selling, weigh terms and head space, not just price: avoid seller financing and long onboarding.
principles.quote: we weren't just optimizing for like cash for example right we were also optimizing for hey how much head space can we gain like immediately
